_comment: Declared blind spots of the quality defence, as measured by scripts/quality_matrix.py.
This file is a registry, not a to-do list: tests/test_quality_matrix.py fails when the
measured set of holes differs from the set declared here, in EITHER direction. A new
blind spot therefore cannot land silently - it has to be written down with an exit
criterion first - and a hole that gets closed cannot stay here as decoration, because
an obsolete entry reads as an open one.
Fields: id = '<kind>:<name>' exactly as measured; opened = date the measurement found
it; exit = the concrete, checkable state that removes it; why = one line of context.
QUALITY_MATRIX.md must list every id in this file and no others.
An empty list is a measured state, not an aspiration: the same gate that fails on an
unregistered hole fails on a registered one the measurement no longer reproduces.

holes.exit: a tests/test_*_suite.py or tests/test_*_spec_table.py asks this surface of something the repository does not own - in practice, the JSON Schema evaluation designed in PR #517 replayed against an official corpus whose source and version are recorded with the result
holes.why: the schema language validate() judges was invented here, so the unit, property and fuzz tiers all ask the engine what it believes, and parity has no second implementation to disagree with

holes.exit: the row's `restricted` list is empty, which `format_matrix()` derives from pyproject.toml: an outside reader whose marker covers every leg this package is tested on (Python 3.8 and 3.14+ included), or a comparison that covers the RFC 8259 dialect on the excluded legs with a stdlib reader the repository does not own and records that JSONC/JSON5 stay schedule-only there
holes.why: orjson and pyjson5 are both declared with `python_version >= '3.9' and python_version < '3.14'` plus armv7l/s390x/ppc64le exclusions, so on the floor leg and on 3.14+ the cross-library module imports nothing and skips, and the leg that compares zero assertions reports the same green as one that compares 198
